problem_statement: The OIC payload parser must reject malformed CBOR payloads and excessive nesting, return an empty representation for an empty array, and release allocated objects on failure.
extra_warnings: Use the supplied tests as the acceptance oracle. Do not add, remove, or modify tests or test helpers.

verification.reason: The statement omits several concrete validation and error-handling requirements that the hidden tests check, but these can be repaired by specifying the public observable behavior without dictating implementation.

problems.detail: The original phrase 'release allocated objects on failure' is ambiguous; the hidden tests call oc_free_rep(rep) after a failed parse, so the parser must leave a freeable representation or NULL rather than have freed it itself.
The tests require an invalid top-level CBOR value that is neither a map nor an array to fail and set *out_rep to NULL.
The tests require map keys to be text strings and require integer keys to be rejected.
The tests require array elements to be homogeneous; mixed arrays such as false/string and integer/map must be rejected.
The tests require string-array items that exceed the item length limit to be rejected.
The tests require a 10-level nested map payload to be rejected, but the statement only says 'excessive nesting' without a threshold.
The tests use MYNEWT_VAL(OC_NUM_REP_OBJECTS) to require failure when more representation objects than the pool are needed, and success at the boundary.
The tests require an empty array to succeed and set *out_rep to NULL.
The tests require an array of maps to be parsed into a linked list of OBJECT oc_rep_t entries with their maps in value_object.

problem_statement_fixed: The OIC payload parser (oc_parse_rep) must reject malformed CBOR payloads and excessive nesting, return an empty representation for an empty array, and release allocated objects on failure. The parser must accept a root that is either a CBOR map or a CBOR array whose elements are all CBOR maps, and must reject any other root and arrays whose elements are not maps. Property keys must be text strings; non-text-string keys must be rejected. Array values must contain elements of one consistent CBOR type; arrays mixing types, such as a boolean and a text string or an integer and a map, must be rejected. A string or byte-string array item whose encoded length is too large for the string-array item limit must be rejected; in particular, a 24-byte text string item in an array must be rejected. Object nesting at depth 10 must be rejected. Truncated CBOR payloads must be rejected. For an empty array, the parser must return 0 and set the output pointer to NULL. Valid maps and arrays of maps must still parse into oc_rep_t representations: an array of maps must produce a linked list of OBJECT representations, and string arrays must be represented as STRING_ARRAY values with the allocated item count and item contents set. If allocation of a representation object fails, including when a map has more than OC_NUM_REP_OBJECTS properties, the parser must return non-zero, and a map with exactly OC_NUM_REP_OBJECTS properties must parse successfully. On any failure, the parser must not leak allocated representation objects and must not leave a pointer to already freed memory; the caller may call oc_free_rep on the returned pointer, which may be NULL. For a root that is neither a map nor an array, the output pointer must be set to NULL.
